items.t: End ‘all military aggression’ against Europe
items.d: US President Donald Trump said Thursday he had asked Vladimir Putin to “pull back all military aggression” against Europe, in a fresh shift in tone towards the Russian leader he called his friend just last week.

items.t: Turkey detains two ex-anchors of seized opposition TV
items.d: Two former anchors at a Turkish opposition broadcaster that was seized by authorities last month have been detained, and an arrest warrant issued for the channel’s news coordinator, Istanbul prosecutors said yesterday.

items.t: Trump calls for probe into ‘fake’ GDP figures
items.d: President Donald Trump called Thursday for an investigation into a routine revision of economic growth figures as he pushed his groundless claims of interference in the US midterm elections.

items.t: Warning shots force US F-16 to retreat
items.d: Iran’s IRGC has claimed that an advanced air defence system yesterday fired warning shots at a US military F-16 fighter jet near Hengam Island, forcing the aircraft to retreat, according to Iranian state media.

items.t: Parliamentary polls: New Zealand PM Luxon loses majority
items.d: New Zealand’s ruling centre-right coalition has narrowly missed winning a parliamentary majority, final election results showed yesterday, leaving Prime Minister Christopher Luxon needing the support of the centrist Opportunity Party to remain in power.

items.t: Eisenkot reaches deal with left-wing faction
items.d: Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party and a left-wing faction agreed on a preliminary coalition deal on Thursday, after a brief dispute that had posed a challenge to his bid to unseat Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu following an inconclusive election last month.
